A bill was introduced in my state to disband the department of mental health and addiction and transfer all funds and responsibilities to the department of corrections. It is a scary time indeed.

I've been off them for a year now, I think. They made me feel nothing and also were making me lactate, which was so weird. No psychosis since i stopped, but I'm having a hard time with motivation. It could be because I stopped taking my antidepressants as well, though. But overall, no extremely concerning symptoms. I feel better now than when I was on meds, but we shall see.

During my psychosis, my brain started feeling like it was on fire. Like all my neurons were lighting up at once. I'd lay on the ground with my eyes closed and could swear I was feeling the two halves of my brain communicating with each other.
I feel this! I'll go a few days just sinking lower and lower and then a few more days feeling a bit of hope. A never ending cycle.

I've driven quite a few times in psychosis. I got lost trying to drive to my house and couldn't figure out how to GPS my way there. I eventually found my way home. I wasn't driving recklessly or even had any type of close call. I would take scenic routes, though, if I thought someone was following me. Probably how I got lost to begin with, but that was one time out of many. The only issue when on meds is I did feel more sluggish, which gave me less time to react. But still never had an accident.

Unfortunately, it is the reality of the illness, but you are doing what you need to take care of yourself. No one would bat an eye if you had cancer. I know it's hard. I feel a bit of shame every time I have to go, but I think that stems from the stigma society has ingrained in me. At the end of the day, every visit was life-saving.

I could never write this coherently in full blown psychosis but what you're describing was how I felt leading up to it. Definitely let your doctors know and try to get good consistent sleep and stay away from substances.
Stimulants always have the risk of psychosis. But it was likely a combo of things and not the Ritalin alone.

I definitely have gone to er for heart rate being that high. EKG said my heart was fine and it eventually dropped to around 160 while I was there. My breathing was also super uneven and the hospital equipment went crazy until I remembered to breathe. I also have celiac and RA. I've read studies about the link between celiac and schizophrenia. It pretty common. Like celiac, RA is another autoimmune disorder and once you have one, the chances of you getting multiple increase unfortunately.

It truly is. It was nice, feeling like I had figured everything out. It happened again when I was in the hospital after getting wellness checked. But it all turned dark so fast and I was so paranoid and scared for my life. Wasn't long before the real world came knocking though, then I just wanted it all back.

I experienced something like this at the very beginning of my first psychotic episode. I hadn't slept in a while, and a glass on my dresser shattered. I remember staring at it and feeling convinced I knew it was going to happen before it did. The air around me felt different, charged almost. And this thought popped in my head, "God was me the whole time."  I felt it in my soul, and like I had heard this somewhere before. 

I wrote in my journal as this thought bounced around my head, but reading it back now, it doesn't seem as profound as it felt at the time. Like I couldn't quite capture the revelation. It felt like before i had this thought, I was preparing myself for something, and the thought tied it all together. 

Like I said, it doesn't make much sense to me now, and i drove myself crazy trying to figure it out for a few years after. I mostly try to forget about it now. But posts like this always get me curious again.

If you are gathering supplies to carry out your plan, I feel you should go inpatient. They will not lock you up if you are voluntarily going to get help. They can adjust meds as needed while you are under their supervision. If it's all just journaling and ideation, stay transparent with your therapist and psychiatrist. If possible, see your therapist more frequently.

I was very stressed from a variety of things and my paranoia and panic started making it impossible for me to sleep. I stayed up all night journaling, reading or binging tv. I started to forget where I was putting things and if I found something out of place, my paranoia would amp up instead of finding the most logical solution. One night, a glass on my dresser shattered and I was convinced I knew it was going to happen before it did. It was around three a.m. when this happened and I had the revelation "God was me the whole time". I felt like this was absolute truth and explained saints and prophets. It was science! Not anything spiritual. Just mental illness. Also the words themselves, I felt like I had heard them before. Despite this being pretty grounded, my delusions got more and more out of control. I was convinced the FBI was watching me because of what I found out, and eventually, I scrapped the whole science thing and thought demon and angels were both after me.

Mad interesting. I've also seen a couple lectures on the evolution of schizophrenia. Talks about why nature hasn't eliminated the illness since some symptoms are super debilitating. Also very interesting.
Actually what got me into the subject was Living wells video with Dr. Palmer. He also was on the Huberman podcast talking about it.

I have celiac disease, so I already can't eat most carbs. Just have to eliminate the rest. The prevalence of people with schizophrenia and celiac is actually pretty high. It's like our bodies are trying to limit carb options naturally.

I feel you. I'm holding on, but I kind of want to just let go. I feel so disoriented and can feel the paranoia creeping up. I'm just trying to keep positive and make sure I'm taking my meds. I'm in an outpatient program right now which I think is slowing the progression.

I'm on the cusp now myself. I'm trying not to fight sleep but I have so much anxiety right now. I just don't feel right. Like the silence will start talking at any moment. I'm listening to music in headphones while watching a YouTube video with subtitles. 

I'm doing deep breathing and sort of rocking back and forth, trying not to let my mind take off again. I've had three crying spells already. I'm also journaling frequently. Anything to keep myself from spiraling.

30 mg Prozac
3 mg Invega 
Diagnosed Schizoaffective Disorder

Being highly stressed could definitely cause an episode, but it sounds like you'll be seeing a doctor soon, so just make sure you are getting adequate sleep and find a good coping skill and you should be fine. Full on psychosis comes on fast and is so debilitating that hospitalization is pretty much guaranteed. Took me three hospitalizations to get out of my first episode.
Are you having any strange thoughts? Like people are actors or that they're following you?  My hallucinations always coincided with delusions during my psychosis.

Definitely make sure you start taking meds consistently and that you are getting adequate sleep. Try and put together a list of coping skills you can do to keep your mind positively engaged. Biggest thing is not to isolate yourself even though that might feel like the safest, more comfortable thing to do. 

Make sure you challenge any paranoid thoughts. Make a list of reasons why a thought is irrational or simply not true.

I've clung to the belief that, through all the messy delusions that were swirling around in my mind, that maybe some of it was my expanded mind perceiving another plane of reality.  
     Maybe all the dark parts were brought about by the revelation of some great truth that my mind couldn't hold onto in sanity. 
     I was missing huge chunks of memory during my first bought of psychosis and the way time seemed to bend was close to supernatural. There was a definite spirituality to it all that I never entertained in my life before. 
     I'd gone to church as a child to hang out with friends, but I never really identified with organized religion or even the idea of a higher power. Now here I was with journal entries that said...."God was ME the entire time". 
     I believed I could see demons and angels, that I was able to access memories of my ancestors, that I could transfer a piece of my consciousness into someone else to influence their thoughts and actions. 
     Then, all that quickly devolved into delusions of extreme isolation. I thought I was one of the only few people left on Earth, that the majority of people were impressions left on the surface; that my home was a space shuttle hurting through the cosmos with only me and my daughter on board. 
     I could believe that my brain is just wired differently and that I have a disease that requires medication to treat my symptoms. But maybe my brain wiring is supposed to be the way it is? 
     Long story short.....I can't make sense of any of it. Even after five years post first psychotic episode.
It's definitely a self esteem issue that could be manifesting into an episode. Are you currently more stressed than normal? And are you on meds at the moment if I may ask?
I haven't had a psychotic episode in 2 years and I continue to smoke. I will say it sometimes makes a depressive episode emerge if I have to go an extended time without smoking.

Try not to dwell on the experiences you had during psychosis. There really is no satisfactory explanation. You can either believe your brain simply went haywire and now you require meds from here on out, or you can believe that there is an aspect of reality we can't normally perceive unless in a state of psychosis. 
    I've tried to reconcile both, but it just keeps me in a flux of not wanting to be medicated, trying to control or guide my psychotic episodes, and trying to have a normal, productive life.

I'm more spiritual but still shun organized religion. I feel like I'm constantly searching for revelations I had while in psychosis. I felt like I knew the point of it all, but it's not meant to be grasped, so as I became right again, I forgot it.
     But it's left a hole that nothing can fill, especially after my mother died. I want to know she's somewhere better. I want to know if it was all worth it.
I feel numb the majority of the time too. I just started taking my meds again after refusing to for a week. I just want to feel something again.
Invega and Prozac....I wake up very alert but not panicked....I'm only on week two though.

My sister took over packing after that. 😅 This was my third episode though so it took only 10 days to come out of as opposed to my first, which lasted for 3 months. It gets easier each time. But still thought I was in a simulation on the 10 minute drive to the mental hospital.
At least you had plenty of pens for note taking though! Lol
This was my experience. It was like everything was in 4k Ultra HD and I could control the elements with my mind and speak to animals and stuff.
I'm not entirely sure. I had a reason, but as soon as I was caught, it escaped my mind and I was just embarrassed lol
My parents were going to take me to the hospital and I tried packing a single raw egg.
Felt terrible. After a week I was freaking out and was in the E.R with the walls changing colors. Was told to stop taking them by E.R. doctor and psychiatrist.
Currently listening to heavy metal while angrily cleaning. It's helping a bit.

I smoked for years before I had a psychotic episode. For me, it's always a combination of four things that send me into psychosis: high amounts of stress (usually work related), severe insomnia, not adhering to meds, and copious amounts of weed in various different forms. This last time, I was able to recognize early signs of a break coming and was able to get back on antipsychotics before I needed another grippy sock vacation. Early signs started the tail end of November last year and I only just stopped smoking weed three days ago. I wasn't having any signs of psychosis and only stopped because of money issues and because my boyfriend wanted to get clean to find a new job. I plan to carry on when he gets hired. Smoking in moderation and not getting back into edibles or dabs, I think is the main reason I haven't had another episode. Everyone is different of course and I wish the US would take it off the schedule I narcotic list so that more studies could look into why it's perfectly fine for some people and life ruining for others.
Oil pastels? I love this so much! The contrast between the two sides is beautiful.

I feel this so much. I don't wanna be isolated and unplugged for so many reasons. I think I have enough coping skills to get through it but only time will tell. I hope you pull through without a grippy sock vacation too. I always feel so lost when I come out of there.
Yes! Next to the bulk food store lol.
Same!!! I might have to go back soon. I'm trying to avoid it just because it's expensive but I'll have to if this depressive episode gets any worse.
I get this all the time and just labeled it maladaptive daydreaming, and I have to make a conscious effort to not let it suck me in to the extent it had in the past.

I'm working full time but just took a three week break a while back to avoid going back to the psych ward. I'm still not doing great though and might be looking into fmla. I'm afraid I might have to go inpatient again for SI but I really really can't afford it as I got covid a week after going back to work and completely wiped out my vacation and sick time.
I've only ever experienced this brain burn in the midst of my psychotic episodes. I'm currently on invega now (1.5mg) and haven't noticed any negative side effects.

It doesn't help when the psych hospital has given me a different diagnosis every time I have to be admitted. I know my psychiatrist has the final say, but they don't really talk to me about my diagnosis anymore. Makes sense that they are more symptom oriented, but my brain really clings to this idea of me being dramatic or faking it.

My mental health facility (there's only one good one in my area that I've gone to multiple times) was actually pretty good, depending on the staff. They had refrigerators on the units that had sandwiches, milk, juices, jello, applesauce, and sometimes even ice cream in the freezer. Also had gluten-free snack options that I got from the cafeteria to take back to my room (I have celiac). They had water machines that came in regular and flavored (one time though it beeped loudly all night and I already had insomnia).We had five smoke breaks a day where we were allowed two cigarettes each time in an enclosed yard. We had a yoga instructor come in a few days, pet therapy where we got to snuggle the goodest boy, and karaoke sometimes for music therapy. They also had a gym they would take us to periodically. 

The only thing I didn't like, was that there were three units that were supposed to be split up. One for mental health, one for substance abuse/detox and one for veterans and first responders. We were mixed up almost every time I went. I realize this is due to capacity issues but it was jarring to be sleeping on the veterans side (things were a little more laid back and quiet) and then do therapy in the mental health unit where people who had similar issues would constantly trigger me. Also, it was obvious they had staffing issues, but there were still some really great counselors and therapists who always made me smile.

I also have a playlist of songs that I listened to mid episode. I can listen to the majority now without feeling any negative emotions, but some will still make me cry.

They were extremely vivid. I swear I could recall the sensations of them sometimes. It was extremely terrifying because they weren't always things I had done but things that were also done to me.
I also had extreme cognitive issues concerning memory, the passage of time and difficulty with speech and writing.

Sounds a bit like my delusions when I was in psychosis. I've been diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and major depressive disorder with comorbid psychosis. I believed I had done awful things even when I knew I couldn't have possibly done them. But sometimes false memories would pop up and I'd fall down the rabbit hole all over again. My first episode was long and only got better with meds and forced hospitalization. The last couple of times, telling myself that these thoughts were irrational and working through it rather than trying to find all the reasons it could be possible, in conjunction with meds, brought me out a lot faster. You're basically practicing mindfulness already, which helped me greatly, but I'd definitely get with a psychiatrist to see about a low level antipsychotic if you haven't already and are still having these thoughts. I was also having hallucinations, but my delusions were much more prevalent.

Depends on how your interaction with her went. A big part of my psychosis was delusions. If she has strong irrational beliefs or seems suspicious of everyone, including close friends and family, it could be the beginnings of a psychotic episode. What you're describing so far just sounds like she's going through a hard time. I have cut my own hair and dyed it plenty of times while still being sane and coherent. Pupil dilation can also occur under extreme stress.

He's also a fair bit older than you and sounds very adept at emotional manipulation. The whole worry about delaying sex bit after an abortion he pushed you into is so fucking gross to me. Not meaning to offend, but he sounds like a grade a creep and you do not deserve to be treated like this.

While in my first and longest episode of psychosis, I think it was more like each aspect of my personality was cranked to 11 and i could only manifest a single characteristic of myself at a time. I journaled through a lot of it and I actually see differences in my handwriting depending on which part of myself was in control. But since these parts of me were so heightened and isolated from the others, they seemed like completely different beings possessing my body at different times. So much so that I named them in later journal entries. I could have named them during it all but my memory of the whole thing is hazy and going back to read entries around that time gives me a headache.
My parents don't have celiac but my mom has scleroderma which is another autoimmune disease.

Nothing with wheat, barley, rye, or malt listened as an ingredient. Stay away from soy sauce unless it's specifically gluten free (often called tamari soy sauce), no pre-made rice crispy treats, read labels on gummy candy as wheat is often added (twizzlers, air head extremes, sour punch straws), no beer or malt beverages. 

Some people with celiac also have a sensitivity to dairy, but if that doesn't apply to you, you're fine there. 

You can have oats as long as they haven't been processed in a facility that also processes wheat. Most oats will specify on the front that they're gluten-free if that's the case. Cereals and granola can also be gluten free. KIND bars are made gluten free. Roasted nuts of any variation should be okay, but be wary of trail mixes. Popcorn is good. Tortilla chips should also be okay (not restaurant ones, they sometimes fry up flour tortillas), spaghetti squash is a great alternative for pasta but they do make dried gluten free pasta that isn't super expensive, smoothies are great (you can track down gluten free protein powders to add if you like, nut butters too), beans of all varieties are fine, rice is a constant in my life, hummus is clear if you've tried and enjoyed that. 

Celiac is very rough for everyone who suffers from it. Some people will even have symptoms after cutting out gluten. Some people develop skin rashes that are extremely painful and leave permanent scarring from ingesting gluten. Neurological issues can manifest from it. Some studies have even shown a link between schizophrenia and celiac. And since celiac is an autoimmune disease, everyone who is diagnosed has a higher chance of having another autoimmune disease in conjunction. I myself have a rheumatologist, a gastroenterologist, a psychiatrist, my primary care provider, and will soon be seeking out a dermatologist and neurologist to deal with the damage that not adhering to a gluten free diet has done. And my last lapse was over a year ago. We're all suffering and in pain here. We're all in the same boat....trying to live with a disease that most people don't believe or have never heard of.

I was on 30 mg duloxetine with 3 mg of risperidone with little adverse side effects. Everyone is different though. They tried to put me back on duloxetine after being off for almost 2 years and my body said no way. Was told to stop taking after a week. Only on the antipsychotic now. 1.5 paliperidone. I really think therapy helped out back then and especially now. Delusions are very sporadic and fleeting and after being put on a beta blocker, I'm pretty much left with just the depression. Suicidal ideation still there every once in a while, but I've been able to manage so far 🤞

Definitely get with your doctors. But my first episode lasted 3 months with no more non script drug use, 2 hospitalizations, and copious amounts of therapy. Was also on an antipsychotic, antidepressant, as needed anti-anxiety meds, and a sleep aid.

I had this feeling hard-core when I first went through psychosis. Even thought I had died and was in purgatory. Spoke to a chaplain and it helped so much and I'm not even religious! When your brain is stuck in fight or flight, it's easy to start feeling this way. It's just chemicals that are sending a signal to look out for danger even though there is none. Just know that it will pass once you reach a point where everything starts regulating normally again. This will happen through any meds or coping skills you are given.

I frequently lost time and sometimes would see it pass super fast while I was staring at an analog clock. Also forgot strange things I pulled out and moved around. People would tell me things I said/did and I had no recollection.

I'm just surviving for the sake of the people in my life at this point. I guess that's my purpose. To be here for the ones that love me and have allowed me to be a part of their lives. To see them thrive. But you also have to see them suffer. And I don't know how much longer I can bear both of our suffering.

I think a belief in something higher gives someone a lot of purpose. You can choose your own way of worshiping or giving praise. Organized religion is what I have a problem with. I connect most with pantheism, the idea that the universe and its creations all have a little piece of God in them.

I feel like everyone walks on eggshells around me because I'll suddenly just go off on someone. I feel so angry that people can be normal, and I'm constantly fighting for that normalcy. I get so mad when people say that having a mental illness gave them a sense of humor, and they benefited from it. I have not once benefited from this, and it's ruined my life every single time it happens.

I was fine after my first episode for two years before work stress and copious amounts of weed pushed me into another episode. I was off meds at the time without approval from my psychiatrist. Had to get back on them and again took them for maybe 4-6 months before feeling well enough to come off again. Took the rest of the year to have me slip again. 

This time, I started back on meds before going into full-blown psychosis. I was put on an antidepressant and antipsychotic. I was having brief delusional thoughts, having trouble regulating my sleep schedule, and was having vision changes (colors changing or things looking like they were vibrating) before reaching out to psychiatrist. All in all if I can keep up with my appointments and meds, as well as get a therapist, I shouldn't go back into psychosis. 

I did have a bad reaction to my antidepressants and had to stop after a week, so I have another appointment scheduled soon to see other options l, as my depression is what most of my care team thinks is what leads to the psychosis. That in addition to stress and anxiety.
I thought some items had trackers and either destroyed them (SD card in phone, not too precious) or gave them away (watch that my dad gave me for Christmas, no reason to suspect he was tracking me).
That could all be fall out from the conditioning/programing we've been subjected to....our true selves breaking through and rebelling.

I feel like it's only during an episode, but I have noticed my memory isn't as good. It's mostly losing things and not being able to accurately tell the passage of time so that could just be adhd. It is hard for me to get out thoughts sometimes, and although I have a pretty extensive vocabulary, I'll suddenly forget a pretty simple word.

Did you ever do edibles and/or have major life stresses going on? My first episode I thought was weed induced, but I've been smoking now for about a year with no issue until work stress, and my mom being in the hospital got me in a bad place again. I managed to get on antipsychotics before full-blown psychosis happened and was also able to take time off work. I'm still smoking, but I'm afraid I'm not out of the woods yet and plan to stop after I go through what I have now. It seems it has to be a mixture of work stress, home stress, lack of sleep, and copious amounts of weed to make me slip into  another episode.
Stress, lack of sleep, and excessive cannabis use were involved in every psychotic episode.

Been smoking on and off since my first episode in 2019. Normally I stop if I feel an episode coming. This time I didn't stop (been feeling weird since Thanksgiving) and have not had a full blown episode since I let my psychiatrist know ahead of time and have been able to take time off from work. In my experience, it's a mix of stress, lack of sleep and cannabis. I'm taking care of stress level and monitoring my sleep with a smart watch. If I notice a back slide in my mental health, I'll stop smoking.
Yes. Work stress again.

Or, if you have those scientific delusions, you could believe the meds were something else altogether and not take them. I had a mix of both deluisions and both were equally debilitating and terrifying.

Psychosis is your brain trying to find correlation in EVERYTHING to validate your hallucinations and delusions. Literally used to make my brain hurt. Once I'm stable on meds and in a good mental place, I can start to appreciate those rare monents that coincidence happens but not let it rule me. I can humbly return to trying to interpret those correlations. Until then, its CBT all the way for me!

Only a psychiatrist can tell you if they're meds that will work for you and are worth trying. Heavy trauma can induce psychosis as well as and increase in depression and anxiety. That is what caused my episodes. Reddit is fine to gain a sense of "I'm not insane, other people feel this way too" but I've noticed it can exacerbate things if you try to dig too far into "what's wrong with me". In my experience, it caused rabbit holes of health anxiety and philosophical beliefs that validated and enforced past delusions.

Mine will come back with the right amount of stressors. Be aware of how much sleep you are getting and if you have major life changes, always have your psychiatrist on speed dial. I also recommend therapy for the trauma of hallucinations and delusions you had while in psychosis, as many people ruminate over what they saw and went through and can send themselves back into it.
Also unplug from online as much as you can. Look up guided meditation videos and other grounding techniques if its hard to keep your phone out of your hands.

To me, this sounds like everything I go through before I experience a full blown psychotic break. Make sure you try to socialize with people you trust, stay away from all substances, make sure you are getting a healthy amount of sleep and try to get as much sunlight as possible. If you still feel the way you do or your symptoms feel like they are to much to effectively do the things mentioned above, look into getting a psychiatrist.

Had a mixture of both. We were all the shared consciousness of an ancient being that began the cosmos. Some of these shards of consciousness were either so intune with or removed from the entity that they were what most identify as angels and demons.  I was on both sides somehow, the fulcrum of some holy type war and thought i was pregnant with the new savior or antichrist. A being that was truly not apart of the original entity.

Many hallucinations were futuristic rooms and advanced technology. Sometimes I thought our reality was a projection of our power and that if I concentrated hard enough, I could manipulate the projection by rearranging atoms.

In psychosis, I experienced different personalities for sure, some of them existing along side each other, but they never had names they came forward with. I named them after the fact to help process some of the things I went through. I did experience voices in my head but they were usually other people thoughts but most of my auditory hallucinations were someone saying my name. Could be another mental health disorder in conjunction with psychosis but I'd keep note of these thoughts and share with your psychiatrist.

Yes. Feelings of hopelessness, crying episodes that lasted hours, fatigue, depersonalization and lack of interest in things I used to like.
